title: Fundamental or Composite? The Higgs Enigma
summary: The discovery of the Higgs boson by the ATLAS and CMS experiments concluded a glorious century of experimental particle physics discoveries, from Rutherford's discovery of the nucleus in 1911, through the discoveries of quarks and leptons from the 1950s to the 1970s, to the discoveries of the weak vector bosons in the 1980s. It cemented the Standard Model of particle physics as providing the viable parameterisation of all sub-atomic observables up to the TeV scale and possibly up to the GUT and Planck scales.
